title: Pick a heatsink for the regulator
story: Heat flow obeys an Ohm's law of its own, so this board is a thermal circuit: volts stand for degrees Celsius, amps for watts and ohms for kelvin per watt. A linear regulator turns 3.5 W into heat (the current source) inside a box at 40 C (the 40 V source). From the junction to the case is 5 K/W and through the thermal pad 0.5 K/W. Choose the heatsink so the junction stays below 110 C (a safe margin under its 125 C limit) and the heatsink itself stays below 85 C.
hints: Temperatures add up like voltages along a chain: Tj = 40 + 3.5 x (5 + 0.5 + theta_SA).
For Tj under 110 C you need 5.5 + theta_SA under 70 / 3.5 = 20 K/W.
A bigger, finned heatsink has a smaller thermal resistance.
